children: NEW YORK CITY, NY /
/ October 30, 2026 /

Rising prices tied to tariffs may have some people watching their budgets more closely. Every dollar can matter when costs continue to climb, as even small fees have the potential to eat into what's left at the end of the month.
That's why some consumers may be rethinking where they keep their money. Choosing the right free checking account can reduce everyday banking costs and free up cash for important expenses.
Here's how the right account can ease some of that financial pressure.
Cut out monthly maintenance fees
Monthly maintenance fees may seem miniscule at first glance. But when they add up over a year or more, they can make a dent in the budget.

Some accounts remove that cost entirely. Certain free checking accounts come with no monthly maintenance fee and no minimum balance requirement. That means account holders can keep more of their money.
Avoid surprise overdraft charges
Overdraft fees may add more stress when finances are already tight. One mistimed payment can trigger an overdraft charge that throws a monthly budget off track.

Some checking accounts offer overdraft protection by letting you link your checking account to a savings or credit account. If a transaction exceeds your available balance, funds are pulled from the linked account to cover the difference - helping you avoid overdraft fees.
A few banks take this a step further. For example, KeyBank's Key Coverage Zone® may waive overdraft fees if an account is overdrawn by a small amount at the end of the day.
When rising prices have already stretched a budget thin, that small buffer could mean the difference between a minor slip and a charge that throws the whole month off track.
Prevent late fees with early direct deposit
When budgets are tight, waiting until payday can mean the difference between paying bills on time or facing a late fee. Getting paid sooner may help account holders stay ahead of due dates.
Some banks offer early direct deposit features that make this possible. By setting this up, account holders could receive their paycheck sooner, offering breathing room when money is short.
Build savings without thinking about it
Setting money aside can feel unrealistic when costs are climbing. But small, automatic transfers can add up without much effort.

One option some banks offer is rounding up debit card purchases. KeyBank's EasyUp®, for instance, can be set to move change and low dollar amounts into your savings each time you swipe your debit card.
If you're watching every dollar because of tariff-driven price hikes, that hands-off approach may help build a cushion without requiring a separate budgeting step.
Reduce costs with easy access to money
Convenient banking services can also help keep costs down. When account holders can access their money easily, they're less likely to run into avoidable fees.

For instance, free access to a large ATM network can help people avoid out-of-network ATM charges. Secure online and mobile banking can also make it easy to deposit checks, pay bills, and send money from anywhere.
Take control of everyday costs

Tariff-driven price increases may be out of most people's control, but banking costs typically don't have to be. Choosing an account with fewer fees and smarter features can help people keep more of their money during uncertain times.
For those feeling the financial pressure, a closer look at their checking account may be a practical first step.
